report: Everyone has agreed on a plan. C reported the office espresso machine is leaking; A preferred a simpler low-maintenance machine and B wanted to keep the old one. Agreed concerns: A is worried about ongoing upkeep; B wants to keep the machine if a repair is straightforward and she has only small slots of free time; C wants coffee working again but cannot coordinate arrangements. Plan: B will note the machine's label (make and model) and where and when it leaks next time she uses it, with no fixed deadline. I will then help arrange a remote diagnosis, so no repair visit slot is needed. If the fix is small and upkeep is manageable, the machine stays; if upkeep remains heavy, the group will revisit A's preference for a simpler replacement. A, B, and C have each confirmed the plan works for them. Next action rests with B, whenever she next uses the machine.
